steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Line the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie plate with a layer of alternating vanilla wafer crumbs and banana slices.

To Make Pudding: In a medium saucepan, combine 1 1/2 cups sugar with flour. Mix well, then stir in half the milk. Beat egg yolks and whisk into sugar mixture. Add remaining milk and butter or margarine.
Place mixture over low heat and cook until thickened, stirring frequently. Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract. Pour half of pudding over vanilla wafer and banana layer while still hot.
Make another layer of alternating vanilla wafers and banana slices on top of pudding layer. Pour remaining pudding over second wafer and banana layer.

To Make Meringue: In a large glass or metal bowl, beat egg whites until foamy. Gradually add 1/4 cup sugar, continuing to beat until whites are stiff. Spread meringue into pie pan, making sure to completely cover pudding layer.
Bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes, just until meringue is browned. Chill before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Banana Pudding Pie
raw_recipe.description: A homemade stovetop pudding is poured over a vanilla wafer crust and sliced bananas, topped with meringue, and baked. This recipe is old and authentic!

video.description: Perfect dessert for a family gathering! Banana slices alternate with vanilla wafers and are covered with creamy and smooth pudding. Topped with a light and sweet meringue, this dessert is as beautiful to look at as much as it is a joy to indulge in!

review.reviewBody: This is the best homemade pudding my husband and I have ever tasted...but please reduce your sugar...I find 1/2 c. sugar to 2 c. whole milk provides just the perfect backdrop for the eggs and vanilla extract to show off their flavors. Oh my goodness, it is really that good!!! My husband and I also think the dish could use more pudding, so next time we will increase milk to 3 c., and adjust sugar accordingly.

I made this and I was not disappointed - in fact it will most likely become a new tradition in my house! I took an entire box of Nilla wafers and made them into crumbs which ended up being more than the 2 cups needed for the recipe. So I decided to use a 9x13 pan but kept all the other ingredients the same. I saw other reviews saying that each bite was 1/2 meringue and I wanted it to be a little more even with the meringue to pudding/crumbs/banana ratio. The only thing I did different was reduce the sugar as suggested by several other reviews (glad I did!) & added banana extract instead of vanilla to the pudding instead (that definitely put it over the top!). I also used the Meringue II recipe from this site for the topping since I've always had good results with it not weeping & it's become my go-to. I plan on making this again but doubling the pudding which will also double the meringue. I also want to try it again with the bottom layer using the crumbs, but make the middle layer with whole Nilla Wafer cookies instead & probably increasing the amount of sliced banana and using a 9x13 again. The pudding is incredible and I will come back to this recipe for any pudding I make in the future - it's that good I promise! Just make sure your egg whites are at room temperature for maximum fluffiness for the meringue. It was gone so fast that I didn't get a chance to take a picture!

Classic banana pudding recipe. I cut the sugar to 3/4 a cup which was plenty sweet for us. I also just did a vanilla wafer crumb topping vs the meringue to save time as it was late in the day and wanted it for dessert. Everyone really enjoyed it on a hot summer evening.

I really enjoyed making this homemade banana pudding. I was so surprised and excited to have something new turn out to be so delectable! My family loved it and it was a great Thanksgiving hit. Like other reviewers, I cut the sugar for the filling in half - mixing in a total of 3/4 cup. Next time I make this, I will double the pudding mixture and double the meringue mixture. I found that with 2-9-inch pie pans, a standard box of Nilla wafers, about 4-5 bananas, and double the amounts of each mentioned above would yield two perfect pudding pies. If I make this in one pan, like an 11x9, I will probably just follow the original measures. So delicious! Thanks for the recipe.
I didn't read the reviews the first time I made this. Mea culpa. The first time it was teeth screeching sweet. I like sweet, but... Wow. I now use 3/4c of sugar. Other than that. It's lovely.

I made this and it was great. After reading reviews I did double the recipe and cut back on the sugar. For a double portion I used 1 1/2 cups of sugar and there was still room to cut back some. I did use ripened bananas so next time I will use 1 1/4 cup of sugar for a double batch. Other than that this recipe was great! It was informative to know from another reviewer that it does take about 10 minutes of continuous whisking before the pudding thickens. I did refrigerate my pudding for 2 hours as others suggested and everything turned out perfect. Great homemade pudding recipe! Thanks Pat!!

I usually never do reviews but I've made this recipe a few times and it just wouldn't be fair to give credit . It is amazing ! I love baked banana pudding . I usually add a little extra flour and milk to make more pudding . After pudding is thick I take it off heat and mush a banana and add it to pudding to give it that banana flavor . Some MISTAKES I've made is making meringe before everything because it turns back to liquid. Also I cut the bananas at the last minute since they brown quickly. I literally feel like I make the best banana pudding . Lasted less than 5 min on thanksgiving table.

I made the pudding part of this recipe for a baked pie crust. I did not make meringue for the topping as this type of pie was requested by a family member who preferred whipped cream topping. After reading the advice of other posters, I used 1 1/4 cup sugar, which was a nice sweetness and wish that I had added 1 more tsp vanilla for a bit richer flavor to match the request of the recipient. This recipe makes enough pudding for a large pie. Everyone was happy!

I made just the pudding part, and as other reviewers suggested, cut the sugar to 3/4 cup. I used a homemade graham cracker crust layered with banana slices, poured the pudding in, and then another layer of banana slices. It came out WONDERFUL.

Yes, a few changes. I used a Nilla Wafer Pie Crust instead of cookies. And I mashed 1 ripe banana into pudding mixture, then I mixed on high while cooking, shaved a 1/4 of cinnamon stick & continued cooking & mixing until thickened. I lined banana slices in bottom of pie crust pour pudding over slices until all bananas are covered. Cut up remaining banana slices into peices, add scarcley on top of pudding. Top & bake

My 92yo dad is from east Tennessee - he said this tasted just like how his mom made it! Following other reviews, I reduced sugar to 3/4 C and added 1/4 tsp of salt. To the egg whites, I added 1/8 tsp cream of tartar. Also, did not crush the wafers - just layered them. Just a note - I cook my homemade puddings on medium (not low), and they turn out nicely.

I grew up watching my mother make this, fascinated by the egg whites turning into meringue, but this is the first time I've ever made it. It didn't turn out right. The pudding didn't thicken up, and the egg whites didn't form a meringue but a golden crust instead, probably because I didn't have granulated sugar so used brown sugar instead. Still, it's the most delicious banana pudding I've ever had, even better than Mom's, and she was the best cook in the neighborhood! Thanks!
I only used a 1/2 cup of sugar
This is literally the closest to my grandmother's recipe I've gotten

I read the reviews and reduced the sugar by half, but it was still too sweet. I should’ve followed reviewer naludson's advice and gone with just 1/2 cup. It’s hard to imagine the original 1.5 cups being enjoyable. I saved the recipe because I like the ease of the pudding and the texture was on point, so thank you for that. I’ll also leave the vanilla wafers whole next time—crushing them didn’t really add anything.
YUMMY THE WHOLE FAMILYS FAVORITE 🥰😍. Thank you guys for such great recipes that are easy to fallow.
My family loved it! It definitely only needs 1/2 cup sugar. I will double the recipe next time!

I love this recipe even though it's the first time making Homemade Banana Pudding Pie. The only thing I changed was to add a couple tablespoons of cream cheese in the pudding. If I do change anything next time, I'll cut down a little on the sugar.
